items.label: text
items.text: The two isomers of propanol can be used toillustrate thesepoints.

items.label: text
items.text: Propan-1-ol has the structure CH-CH2-CH2-OH. There are eighthydrogenatoms,infourdifferentchemicalenvironments. YoumightthinkthatthetwopairsofhydrogenatomsintheCH2 groups are in the same chemical environment, but they are not. The first CH2 group is joined to CH, and CH2, but the second oneis joined toCH2and OH,and these are different chemical environments.Thismeansthatthereshouldbefourpeaksinthe spectrum. Fig A shows the low resolution H NMR spectrum of thisisomerwith anintegration trace.

items.label: text
items.text: Propan-2-ol has the structure CHs-CH(OH)-CH3. There are eight hydrogen atoms,butthoseinthetwoCHgroups areinthesame chemical environments.ThisisbecauseeachCHgroupisjoined to CH(OH)CH3. The hydrogen atoms in the CH group and in the OH group are in unique chemical environments. This means that there should be three peaks in the spectrum.FigB shows the low resolutionHNMRspectrumofthisisomerwiththeratioofpeak areasindicatedbycircled numbers.
